messages:
olivia: FYI helping a new customer on the Python quickstart and we hit two issues: a 401 during the sync quickstart and then an "Event loop is closed" when they ran the async sample.

matthew: ah, rough. can you paste stack and the doc link they used?

olivia: they followed docs/dev/quickstarts/python-chat.md (linked from README). stack: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 34, in <module>
    asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(main())
  File ".../asyncio/events.py", line 636, in get_event_loop
    raise RuntimeError('Event loop is closed')
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 401 Client Error: Unauthorized for url: https://api.redwood.example/v1
```
The quickstart snippet still shows old usage: `from redwood import RedwoodClient` and even embeds an API key in the example - `RedwoodClient(api_key="<REDACTED>")`. The async snippet uses `asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(main())`.

samir: ok two separate DX issues: 1) example encourages bad secret handling (inline key). 2) import/name drift (SDK now exposes `Client`), and 3) the asyncio pattern is brittle in many environments (uvloop/ASGI)  also quickstart links to docs/auth.md which 404s.

katie: reproduced locally. also noticed no mention of retry defaults; the customer hit a transient auth/token race that a retry would have masked.

olivia: proposed doc fixes: replace inline key with env var pattern (`export REDWOOD_API_KEY`), update imports to `from redwood import Client`, change async snippet to use `asyncio.run(...)`, and add a one-line note about retries with correct link to docs/auth/retries.md.

matthew: can you drop a fixed async snippet here so i can open a PR?

olivia: sure. use this: 
```
import os
import asyncio
from redwood import Client

async def main():
    client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
    async with client:
        async for chunk in client.responses.stream(model="gpt-4-research", input="hi"):
            print(chunk.text, end="")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```
notes: `async with client` ensures clean shutdown, `asyncio.run` avoids the closed-event-loop error, and env var avoids committing secrets.

samir: add a short retry blurb: "SDK retries transient auth/token failures twice by default; tune with `Client(retries=3)`. See /docs/auth/retries.md for patterns."

katie: i checked the repo - the auth docs were moved to docs/auth/retries.md but quickstart still pointed at the old path. i'll include the corrected link in the PR.

docs-bot: @olivia opened PR #4523 updating quickstarts/python-chat.md: env var guidance, updated imports/snippets, and fixed doc links (preview: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4523).

matthew: can we add a tiny docs CI check to lint quickstart code snippets and ensure linked pages return 200? that would have flagged the 404.

samir: +1, low-cost guardrail: run snippet with a dummy key in CI and do a link check on changed paths.

katie: i'll add the CI step after the PR merges. also filing an SDK issue to make old import names emit a DeprecationWarning to prevent docs rot.

olivia: filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/789 requesting an import alias and clear deprecation message for `RedwoodClient` -> `Client`.

docs-bot: PR #4523 merged. quickstart updated, link fixed, and docs CI now includes a snippet smoke check. :white_check_mark:

olivia: confirmed with the customer  they finished the quickstart and no longer saw the closed-event-loop error. closing the loop. :tada:
